title: Design System: Live to Eat Food

display.purpose: One per page: the page's big promise or a place name.

title.purpose: Card titles, deal amounts, merch lines, the hero line.

title-sm.purpose: Place names in lists, small sticker titles; Bagel never below 20px.

body.purpose: Everything people read, max 68ch; 16px floor on phones.

meta.purpose: Cuisine, neighbourhood, price, distance, captions, in olive.

tag.purpose: Chips, ratio tags, table heads, labels on stickers; never sentences.

hand.purpose: One line in Tina's own words, tomato, never invented.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: Stickers, panels, buttons, current nav item, phone UI pieces.

shadows.name: lift-hi
shadows.purpose: Peeled (hovered) link stickers and the phone mockup frame.

shadows.name: kiss-cut
shadows.purpose: Printed kiss-cut ring prepended to lift on every white sticker surface; merch items use 6px / 7.5px.

shadows.name: button-rim
shadows.purpose: White vinyl rim around the primary pill button, prepended to lift.

shadows.name: food-drop
shadows.purpose: filter for SVG food stickers that carry their own white die-cut border.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The single easing for all state transitions.

motion.name: peel
motion.value: transform .5s, box-shadow .5s / filter .5s; hover: rotate(tilt - 3deg) translateY(-4px) scale(1.03)
motion.purpose: The one authored motion: a sticker lifts a corner on hover (hover-capable pointers only).

motion.name: button
motion.value: transform .4s, box-shadow .4s, background-color .2s; hover: translateY(-2px) rotate(-1deg)

motion.name: roulette-spin
motion.purpose: Restaurant Roulette wheel, about 4-5 turns; the only spinning element.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: transition: none; animation: none; scroll-behavior: auto

narrative.overview:
Every mark, label and food illustration in this system is a die-cut sticker you could peel off a sheet and put on a laptop, a takeout bag or a hoodie. A page is a stack of rounded pastel backing sheets (butter, lemon, pistachio, peach, white vinyl, one dark basil sheet), each carrying the printer's evidence of a real sheet: faint registration marks in all four corners and a small slug line along the bottom edge naming the sheet. Content sits on those sheets as white vinyl stickers, each with a printed kiss-cut ring around it and a soft lift off the paper.

The personality runs warm, then playful, then trustworthy. Warmth comes from butter-and-lemon daylight and one deep basil ink that carries every word. Play comes from a chunky rounded display face, small deliberate tilts and a scatter of food stickers around (never over) content. Trust is carried by a strict label system: Tina's handwriting in tomato means she ate there and paid; sponsors get a hatched oat tag with the word "Sponsored" and no stickers at all.

Density is relaxed and generous: big sheet padding, 30px grid gaps, one field colour per sheet. Food is the only illustration subject. The retired Worcester streetscape, triple-decker motif and asphalt-and-mustard palette are confirmed rejections and do not return.
keyCharacteristics: Rounded pastel backing sheets stacked down the page, each with corner registration marks and a bottom slug.
White vinyl stickers with a printed kiss-cut ring and a soft basil-tinted lift.
One ink: basil green carries all text and outlines; pastels are grounds and fills only.
Four type voices with fixed jobs: Bagel Fat One shouts, Figtree reads, Bricolage Grotesque labels, Shantell Sans is Tina's hand.
Flat-colour food stickers with a 4u basil outline and a 9u white die-cut border.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: Text is basil (or olive for secondary, leaf for links, tomato for Tina's hand). White text appears only on basil or leaf. White or pale text on a pastel never ships: white on lemon is 1.2:1.

rules.name: The One Field Per Sheet Rule
rules.body: One field colour owns a whole sheet; pastels are never striped inside a section. Roughly 60% butter or vinyl, 25% one other pastel field, 10% basil, 5% yolk, tomato and illustration colour.

rules.name: The Tomato Means Tina Rule
rules.body: Tomato signals only that Tina wrote it. It never marks a sale, an alert, an error or an ad, and never sets body copy on a pastel.

rules.name: The Four Voices Rule
rules.body: Each face has one job and two roles never mix inside one element. Bagel shouts, Figtree reads, Bricolage labels, Shantell is Tina.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Headings and buttons are sentence case. All caps live only in artwork (the stamp rim, tiny printed tags inside the Woo-pon ticket, decal and punch card), never in screen UI.

rules.name: The Tabular Facts Rule
rules.body: Prices, times, hex codes and tables use tabular numerals. Bagel tracks at −0.01em; everything else at 0.

rules.name: The Kiss-Cut Rule
rules.body: Every white sticker surface on a sheet gets the kiss-cut ring in the sheet's own field colour. A white box with only a drop shadow is not a sticker.

rules.name: The Peel Rule
rules.body: The only authored motion: on hover a sticker lifts 4px, turns 3° further and scales 1.03 while its shadow deepens (500ms, `cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1)`). The roulette wheel spin is the one functional exception. No scroll-triggered entrances; nothing is hidden at rest; `prefers-reduced-motion` removes all transitions.

dos: Do set basil text on every pastel field; it clears AA everywhere (9.8:1 on lemon, 11.3:1 on butter).
Do give every white sticker surface the kiss-cut ring in its sheet's field colour plus the Lift shadow.
Do let one field colour own each sheet, and use peach on one sheet per page at most.
Do keep earned and paid visibly different: hand and tomato for Tina, hatch, oat and the word "Sponsored" for paid spots.
Do pair every label, badge and verdict with a word and an icon.
Do draw food stickers on a 120u square with a 4u basil outline, round joins, a 9u white die-cut border, two or three flat fills and at most one white highlight at about −30°.
Do vary sticker tilts between −8° and +8°, never two neighbours at the same angle, and keep the wordmark within 3°.
donts: Don't set white or pale text on a pastel; white on lemon is 1.2:1.
Don't use tomato for anything but Tina's hand: not buttons, links, sales, errors or alerts.
Don't put the stamp, Tina's handwriting or a quote in her voice on a sponsored placement, and give sponsored modules no stickers.
Don't rate with stars or numbers; use Tina's verdicts in words.
Don't place stickers over food photos, prices, labels or body text; they go around content, on the field.
Don't stretch, squash or recolour the wordmark, recolour its egg o's or split its lines.
Don't bring back houses, streetscapes, skylines or city clip-art, or the asphalt-and-mustard palette.
Don't set Bagel Fat One below 20px or for paragraphs, or set screen UI in all caps.
Don't add gradients, textures or shading to food stickers, or faces on food.
